text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The killer of industrialist Ozdemir Sabanci confesses that he also took part in the murder of two soldiers in an attack on an Istanbul gendermarie post in 1995.
- Israel invites Turkish soldiers to monitor conditions in Hebron after Israeli troops pull out.
- Police say Sabanci's killer did not surrender to the Turkish embassy in Damascus as other officials have said. He was arrested in cooperation with the Syrian intelligence service.
- The government will give the go ahead on Wednesday for a huge project to support agriculture and cattle breeding project in eastern Turkey.
- Iraqi Kurdish faction leader Jalal Talabani begins dialogue with Iraqi President Saddam Hussein after his rival Massoud Barzani also moved closer to Baghdad.
- Three members of a police anti-terror team will be arrested because they did not give statements to a parliamentary commission probing a security scandal.
- Constitutional court to decide on January 21 whether to allow the sale of Turk Telekom.
- Islamic sects sexually exploite young girls.
- Turkish Industrialists and Businessmen Association (TUSIAD) names Muharrem Kayhan as its candidate for the association's chief executive post.
- Casinos will be outlawed in six months. Draft law for the closure of the casinos being studied by the cabinet.
